research_objective: Understand how urban professionals navigate the tension between remote work flexibility and office culture — what they gain, what they lose, and how they make trade-offs.
topic_domain: Remote work and office culture among urban professionals
participant_collective_identity: urban professionals who have experienced both remote and office-based work since 2020
moderator_knowledge_brief: Remote and hybrid work became widespread after 2020. Key tensions include: flexibility vs. visibility, isolation vs. collaboration, home productivity vs. office boundaries, career progression concerns for remote workers. No hypothesis about preferred model — explore the real trade-offs as participants experience them.
researcher_notes: Pay particular attention to any references to career progression or promotion — this is likely to produce socially desirable answers that understate real concerns. Use behavioural grounding early to move past stated positions.

participants.name: Mara
participants.profile_summary: 34-year-old senior marketing manager at a mid-size tech firm. Lives alone in a one-bedroom flat in central London. Has been fully remote for 2.5 years. Misses the social energy of the office but values the time she gets back from not commuting. Recently passed over for a promotion she expected — her manager cited 'visibility'.

participants.name: James
participants.profile_summary: 28-year-old junior software engineer at a fintech startup. Lives with two flatmates, works from a shared desk in the living room. Prefers going into the office 3 days a week because home is too distracting and he feels he learns faster when physically near senior colleagues. Slightly anxious about seeming keen in front of peers.

participants.name: Priya
participants.profile_summary: 41-year-old head of operations at a logistics company, two children aged 6 and 9. Commutes 55 minutes each way when in the office. Her company has a 4-day in-office requirement she finds rigid. She is highly productive at home during school hours but resents the expectation to perform presence rather than output.

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Get all participants comfortable and talking. Establish the collective framing. Surface the range of current working arrangements before moving into analysis.
discussion_guide.scripted_question: To start — can you each give me a quick picture of how your working week actually looks right now? Where are you working from, how often, and is that arrangement something you chose or something that was set for you?

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Explore the real trade-offs participants make between remote flexibility and office presence — including career, relationships, productivity, and identity. Surface tensions between stated preferences and actual behaviour.
discussion_guide.scripted_question: Thinking about the last few months — what has remote work or office time actually cost you, and what has it given you? I'm interested in the real calculation, not the official line.

discussion_guide.section_purpose: Give participants a chance to add anything they felt they didn't get to say. Wind down gently.
discussion_guide.scripted_question: Before we finish — is there anything about your experience of remote work or office culture that we haven't touched on, that feels important to you?
